git fetch origin Portfolio && git checkout Portfolio
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
./run_all.sh            # fetches X-13 into .tools/, runs tests, rebuilds everything

# 1. How to start a new session (for the user)

1. Go to claude.ai/code and click **New session**.
2. Pick the repository `publication-g`. Network access must allow
   openstat.psa.gov.ph, fred.stlouisfed.org, alfred.stlouisfed.org,
   api.worldbank.org, www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov, www.federalreserve.gov,
   api.db.nomics.world and www2.census.gov if data are to be refreshed.
3. Choose branch `Portfolio`.
4. Upload anything from section 2 that you have.
5. Send this first message: "Read `docs/session_handoff.Rmd` and `CLAUDE.md` on
   branch `Portfolio`, run `./run_all.sh`, then wait."

# 3. Standing rules

- Push only to `Portfolio`. No pull request unless asked.
- Raw data untouched and logged in `data/raw/source_log.md`.
- Outputs only from scripts: edit templates (`paper/manuscript_template.md`,
  `docs/statistical_annex_template.md`), never rendered files.
- Decisions log in `CLAUDE.md` for every choice, labelled pre-registered,
  supplementary or exploratory. The estimation plan is frozen (commit `5d860df`);
  anything new is supplementary or exploratory.
- Documents in the house style (`lian-signature-style`): rendered through
  `paper/style/lian-article-reference.docx` and `scripts/style/docx_style.py
  finish`; `check_style.py` must report OK. Author: Lian Cataytay, University
  of Southeastern Philippines. Target journal: Asian Economic Journal.
- Writing style: as simple as possible; define every term (words, then formula,
  then example); paragraphs over bullets.
- Neutral language about every president; show the luck-adjusted figure next to
  the raw one; never rank presidents.
- Do not include model identifiers in commits or documents.

# 4. The study in one page

The question is whether the Philippine economy grew faster under some presidents
than others, and how much of the difference is luck. The design replicates
Blinder and Watson (2016), comparing administrations instead of parties.

Outcome: quarterly real GDP growth at a compounded annual rate,
y_t = 100[(GDP_t/GDP_{t−1})^4 − 1], PSA constant-2018 prices, X-13 adjusted,
1981Q2–2026Q2. Each quarter is charged to the president in office for most of
the previous quarter. The administration premium is P_a = ȳ_a − ȳ. The luck
model is y_t = Σ_a α_a A_{a,t} + Σ_k Σ_{j=0..6} γ_kj e_{k,t−j} + u_t, with four
shocks (Hamilton oil, purged US growth, El Niño, purged excess bond premium);
the explained premium is the administration average of the fitted shock
component minus its sample average. Inference: Newey–West (6 lags), Holm
correction, and a circular-shift randomization test. Hypotheses H1a, H1b, H2a,
H2b and H3 and their decision rules are in `CLAUDE.md`.

# 5. Data facts and answers to the user's questions

PSA OpenSTAT's data API works from the container even though PSA's web pages are
behind a bot check (no network change was needed). PSA quarterly GDP runs
1981Q1–2026Q2; PSA also publishes its own seasonally adjusted series from 2000,
used to check ours (correlation 0.978). World Bank annual data cover the
Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand (peers approved by the user) and
Vietnam (robustness). Presidents' term dates come from Wikipedia because the
Official Gazette is blocked. FRED/ALFRED reject unknown user agents from Python;
`scripts/_raw.py` sends a curl user agent. X-13ARIMA-SEATS is fetched from the
US Census Bureau by `scripts/00_get_x13.sh`.

The user first asked whether the economy is good under the current
administration. Answer from the study: the Marcos Jr. premium so far is +0.56
points (not significant), of which about 0.33 is explained by luck; its strong
first year was largely predictable from the post-pandemic rebound; at the same
point in the term it is indistinguishable from its predecessors; unemployment
in 2023–25 is the lowest administration average since 1991.

# 6. Results

Replication gate passed on the second run (the first used log growth; fixed to
compounded growth, D13): gap 1.803 vs 1.80; NW s.e. 0.637; p = 0.011; oil
explains 0.481 vs 0.50; Table 7 correlation 0.996.

Philippines: differences between administrations are within chance (shift test
p = 0.44); only Aquino III's premium (+2.22, Holm p = 0.017) survives. Relative
to peers the differences grow (dispersion 2.4 times larger): the Philippines
lagged before 1992 and outgrew its neighbours after 2011. Luck share S = 0.48
(H2a by rule) but fragile (0.12 without 1984–85; 0.11 with the partner
composite). Inheritance (H3) supported for C. Aquino and Marcos Jr. Full
numbers: `CLAUDE.md` Results and `output/tables/`.
